(i) the COF of both bearing materials decreases with the applied pressure, (ii) the specific wear rate of both bearing materials increases with sliding speed and (iii) the specific wear rates are higher at low pressure.

, under dry friction conditions, the coefficient of sliding friction is decreasing with increasing normal pressure and increasing with increasing sliding speed, and the specific wear rate coefficient is decreasing with increasing pressure and increasing with sliding speed.

the bearing material with a higher content of solid lubricants (Orkot) is more resistant to wear and has a lower coefficient of friction compared to the bearing material with less solid lubricant (ThorPlas).

, for the studied bearing materials, the friction and wear are mainly governed by the pressure, while the sliding speed has only a secondary influence.
